It's Black Friday week and the Apple discounts keep on coming! If you're after a new MacBook, Apple Watch, iPad, or a different piece of Apple gear, then now is the best time to buy, as we're seeing some absolutely killer deals.
Take the always-in-demand MacBook Neo, which has received one of its first major discounts since the price rose to $699 earlier in the year. It's currently available for just $649 at Amazon. If you need a machine with a little more power, then there are also big savings to be had on various MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.
Deals don't stick around forever, and some are selling out quickly, so act fast if you see something that you like here.
We'll be on hand all day today, November 25, to bring you the best Apple deals we can find, so keep checking back to see what's new.
iPhone 18 Pro: free w/ new line + unlimited @ T-Mobile T-Mobile is offering the iPhone 18 Pro for free when you open a new line and use three T-Mobile Picks. (T-Mobile's new data plans offer up to 3 Picks or free perks, such as DashPass by DoorDash or Netflix Standard. The number of Picks you get is based on the plan's price or how many phone lines are on your plan). In our iPhone 18 Pro review , we said it's the best phone money can buy. The iPhone 18 Pro features a 6.3-inch OLED 120Hz display (2622 x 1206), A20 Pro chipset, and 256GB of storage. You also get a 48MP main, 48MP ultrawide, 48MP telephoto lens w/ 4x zoom, and an 18MP front camera.
In our AirPods Pro 3 review, we said these earbuds are the best AirPods yet. With features like Live Translation, heart rate tracking, and integrated Siri, they're ideal if you want your earbuds to work for you. But if you "just" want industry-leading earbuds with perfect sound and great ANC, the Pro 3 won't let you down.
Price check: $149 @ Walmart | Sold out @ Amazon
Apple Watch Series 12 delivers the line's most accurate heart rate sensing yet, alongside a suite of advanced health and fitness features. It's powered by Apple's new S11 chip, which enables new Audio Intelligence features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
I didn't expect to see this deal. The new iPad mini A20 Pro is $100 off. The new model sports a larger 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR Display (2316 x 1512), A20 Pro CPU, 24% smaller bezels than its predecessor, and better audio. You also get a 12MP camera on the front and back and Wi-Fi 7 support. The base models (128GB/256GB) boast a 5-core CPU with 2 super cores and 3 efficiency cores, whereas the 512GB model bumps it to a 6-core CPU with 2 super cores and 4 efficiency cores. This is the first time it's on sale.
The Mac mini M6 keeps the ultra-compact 5x5-inch design introduced with the prior generation, but packs major performance upgrades under the hood. You get the raw speed of Apple's M6 chip, upgraded graphics with hardware-accelerated ray tracing for better 1080p gaming, 16GB of unified memory, and improved connectivity thanks to Apple's custom N1 chip, which adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, and Thread support.
Apple doesn't do discounts, so buying from the Apple Store always means you're paying full price. This doesn't mean the company is ignoring Black Friday. As is the case in previous years, the Apple Store Black Friday Event 2026 will see Apple give out gift cards to everyone buying eligible products.
Buying an iPhone or Apple Watch nets you a $100 gift card, while eligible iPads will come bundled with a $125 gift card. AirPods and Beats buyers get $75 back, while HomePods and eligible accessories will come with $50 and $25 gift cards, respectively. The largest gift card on offer is $300, which can be yours if you're buying an eligible Mac.
This obviously means you're paying full price, but you can always put that gift card to good use later — including buying accessories or spending it in the App Store.
Apple's Black Friday Event runs from November 27 to 30, and you can check out all the eligible products on the Apple Store website.
When it comes to overall quality, Apple TV is easily the best streaming service around. The catalogue may not be as large as the likes of Netflix or Disney Plus, but the shows and movies on offer are second to none.
Which is why you can't miss out on the fact Apple has slashed the price in half for six months, dropping from $14 a month to just $7.
On offer are the known favorites like Ted Lasso, Slow Horses and For All Mankind, but there are some hidden gems you may not have noticed. By son is a big fan of Shape Island, while I'm partial to Shrinking and Silo. Foundation is also on my watch list, because I've only heard good things about the adaptation Asimov's acclaimed series.
Apple TV: was $14 a month, now $7 a month for six months
Unfortunately, I can't tell you that Verizon has knocked a ton of money off the excellent iPhone 18 Pro for Black Friday. But, if you sign up for a three-year Simplicity Plus or Simplicity Pro plan, you do get a free Apple Watch Series 12 and an iPad 11.
That's not a deal to turn your nose up at, since these two accessories would cost you $898 if you bought them separately at full price. You will need a Verizon service plan to claim them both for free, though.
I'm not going to lie: I'd like to see a larger discount than just $50 on the A16 iPad 11-inch. But at the same time, if I was going to recommend and iPad to most people, it would be this one. You get a bright Liquid Retina display, a 10-hour battery life, and you can accessorize it with the Apple Folio keyboard or Apple Pencil.
If you just want a tablet for a bit of light productivity alongside listening alongside your regular media consumption, then there's no reason not to pick this one. Especially as you can pocket $50 with this Best Buy deal.
RAMageddon may have driven up the price of one of our favorite laptops, but the MacBook Neo just got a nice discount for Black Friday!
The specs sound a bit bizarre on paper – an a18 Pro out of an iPhone and 8GB of RAM. But as it turns out, macOS is so well optimized that this is all you need for a sleek, zippy experience.
This is an ideal productivity machine for students and those on a budget who don’t want to give up those premium niceties like an aluminium design.
I don't have personal experience with the AirPods Max 2... but I've used their predecessor for years and can vouch for the quality of Apple's over-ears efforts. My colleague Erin reviewed the AirPods Max 2 back in March and praised the bright, energetic mids and melodic, controlled bass.
The design hasn't changed from the first generation, so while they are a bit on the heavy side, the AirPods Max 2 spread the weight nicely with the mesh headband. As with the AirPods Pro 3, the real benefit of these is Apple's multi-pairing. You can go from listening to music on your iPhone to watching a video on your iPad in a heartbeat. I've never been crazy about the price, but then this Black Friday deal is a big step back in the right direction.
I have AirTags for everything. I have them on two different sets of keys, in my backpack, attached to my bike and, of course, one stashed safely away in my wallet. And I've never paid full price for any of them.
Right now, you can grab four AirTags for $79, down from the usual price of $99. That works out at under $20 per AirTag. This is a deal that comes round most years on retail events like Black Friday and it's always worth taking advantage of.

articles.title_orig: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
articles.title_zh: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration said it will issue a new wave of tariffs on China and other major U.S. trading partners, the latest escalation in global trade tensions.
The U.S. will increase tariffs on Chinese goods by an additional 20%, while also raising import taxes on goods from the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan and India.
The planned tariffs are meant to curtail trade practices that the U.S. says undercut American companies, including what the White House has called excessive manufacturing output from those economies.
"For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market-distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America's manufacturing base," Ambassador Jamieson Greer, the U.S. Trade Representative, said in a statement .
The announcement came after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) completed a series of months-long investigations into the trade practices of 12 countries, the 27-member EU and the self-governing island of Taiwan.
In a call with reporters late Tuesday, a senior administration official said the tariffs are in the proposal phase and did not provide an implementation timeline.
The planned tariffs would be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which authorizes the USTR to investigate trade agreements if they violate existing deals, are not justified by market forces, or actively discriminate against American goods.
Tariffs are taxes on imported goods. They raise costs for businesses, which sometimes pass the burden onto consumers in the form of higher prices.
The White House moved to implement the tariffs despite mounting frustration among U.S. voters about rising costs. In a CBS News poll conducted after the midterms, 66% of respondents said President Trump's tariffs have hurt the national economy.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: China's Hansoh Pharma strikes drug deal with Bayer unit worth nearly $3.3 billion
articles.content_orig:
China Southern Airlines said in a filing late Tuesday that its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines had agreed to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft with a combined catalog price of approximately $7.4 billion.
The announcement comes after President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he expected China to purchase another 250 Boeing aircraft, following his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit last week.
"By the way, I sold 250 Boeings to China, and I think they're going to do another 250," Trump said.
In May, China approved an initial purchase of 200 Boeing aircraft for Chinese airlines following Trump's visit to Beijing, marking the country's first commitment to purchase U.S.-made Boeing aircraft since 2017, according to the White House.
It was not immediately clear whether Xiamen Airlines' latest purchase was part of that commitment.
China Southern, which owns a 55% stake in Xiamen Airlines, said the actual purchase price would be lower than the combined list price because of discounts offered by Boeing. The company did not disclose the final purchase price, citing confidentiality provisions in the agreement.
The aircraft are scheduled to be delivered in batches between 2031 and 2034, with the purchase financed through a combination of internal funds and external financing, the filing showed. The transaction remains subject to shareholder and relevant Chinese government approvals.
China Southern said the purchase would support Xiamen Airlines' planned relocation to the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport and the expansion of its route network.
The agreement follows the group's recent purchase agreement for 137 Airbus A320neo - family aircraft, the filing showed. China Southern said sourcing aircraft from different manufacturers would help diversify its fleet and improve operational flexibility.
Other Asian carriers, including Philippine Airlines and Malaysia Aviation Group , have also announced Boeing aircraft orders this month.

articles.title_orig: Benjamin Netanyahu trial judges suggest dropping Case 4000 with Attorney-General in attendance
articles.title_zh: Benjamin Netanyahu trial judges suggest dropping Case 4000 with Attorney-General in attendance
articles.content_orig:
The judges in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s criminal trial urged prosecutors on Wednesday to consider dropping the Case 4000 count against him and questioned whether the conduct alleged in Case 2000 constitutes a criminal offense, as Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara appeared before them for the first time.
The Jerusalem District Court panel said the completion of Netanyahu’s testimony had brought the proceedings to a point requiring a fresh assessment; its doubts extended beyond the bribery charge it had previously urged prosecutors to reconsider.
“In our view, the public interest requires a rethink,” Judges Rivka Friedman-Feldman, in remarks delivered on behalf of herself, and Judges Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham.
The judges emphasized that their comments reflected their impressions so far - not a verdict - and concerned Netanyahu alone, since they had not yet heard the other defendants’ testimony.
The discussion came amid coalition negotiations following the election, including talks between Likud and Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party over forming a new government. That gives the prospect of an agreement ending Netanyahu’s trial political significance beyond the courtroom. The judges did not link their proposals to those negotiations.
The proceedings also face a practical time constraint: Friedman-Feldman, who heads the panel, is due to retire in March 2028. With defense testimony still underway, time is also needed for closing arguments and the writing of a verdict, adding urgency to the effort to bring the trial toward a conclusion.
Baharav-Miara defended the prosecution team and said the court’s comments would be examined. She outlined two ways to conclude the case: a verdict or an agreement reflecting the nature of the alleged conduct and offenses.
She reiterated that the prosecution had responded positively to President Isaac Herzog’s initiative for talks, while the other side had yet to respond. Netanyahu’s lawyer, Amit Hadad, called for criminal mediation.
Hadad proposed sitting down with Baharav-Miara behind closed doors at the courthouse to discuss a possible agreement.
On Case 1000, concerning gifts from wealthy businessmen and Netanyahu’s alleged actions to advance one donor’s interests, the judges said most of the evidence was already before them, subject to a request to take testimony abroad from James Packer. They proposed finding a procedural route to conclude that count and reach a decision.
Unlike their comments on Cases 4000 and 2000, the judges did not express comparable doubts about Case 1000, instead calling for a path toward its conclusion. A plea agreement would not necessarily resolve the question of Netanyahu’s political future: a conviction based on an admission could still raise the issue of moral turpitude and its consequences for his eligibility to hold public office.
In Case 4000, prosecutors allege that Netanyahu advanced regulatory decisions benefiting telecommunications company Bezeq and its then-controlling shareholder, Shaul Elovitch, in exchange for favorable treatment on the Walla news site, which Elovitch also controlled.
The judges identified difficulties on both sides of that alleged exchange.
The claim that Netanyahu instructed then-Communications Ministry director-general Shlomo Filber to act in Bezeq’s favor rested largely on Filber’s testimony, they said. They questioned whether factual findings could be based on that account, citing the course of his questioning, changes in his version and objective information inconsistent with it.
The judges’ remarks did not specifically address the testimony of former Netanyahu aide Nir Hefetz, another prominent prosecution witness in Case 4000 .
They also expressed serious doubt that prosecutors had established the alleged “unusual responsiveness” to coverage requests, questioning the comparison against which that responsiveness was being measured. Separately, they doubted whether Netanyahu’s awareness of such treatment at the time had been proved.
Those doubts also affected the alleged conflict of interest underlying the breach-of-trust accusation, the panel said.
“Regarding this count, we assess that the prospects of conviction are low, to a degree that justifies reconsidering the matter,” the judges said.
Their proposal to consider withdrawing the first count therefore went further than their earlier recommendations, in June 2023 and again this June, to reconsider the bribery charge.
The judges expressly limited their assessment to Netanyahu; withdrawing the charges against him would not automatically end the bribery prosecution against Shaul and Iris Elovitch, whose liability would require separate consideration.
Case 2000 concerns Netanyahu’s discussions with Yediot Aharonot publisher Arnon Mozes about favorable coverage in exchange for steps against rival newspaper Israel Hayom .
Here, the judges questioned whether the facts alleged in the indictment and the evidence presented supported the prosecution’s legal conclusions. The accusation concerns Netanyahu’s continued engagement with Mozes’s proposal and actions allegedly presenting a genuine possibility that he would use his office to advance legislation benefiting the publisher.
The panel said prosecutors should have an opportunity to present a structured legal argument before a decision on how to proceed, including on the allegation that Netanyahu used the power of his office to obtain a personal benefit.
The panel explained that Baharav-Miara had been summoned because the attorney-general bears responsibility for decisions on continuing the prosecution. It explicitly said the summons expressed no lack of confidence in the prosecutors appearing before it.
The trial began in May 2020. Netanyahu faces fraud and breach-of-trust charges in all three cases and bribery in Case 4000. He denies wrongdoing.
Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
articles.title_zh: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
articles.content_orig:
The party of Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing party in a bid to form the next government following October’s elections .
The centrist Yashar party said on Tuesday that it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.
After no bloc managed to secure a 61-seat majority, Israel’s parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government.
President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming ⁠a government, while Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister despite the October 27 election stripping him of his majority.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.
The right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.
Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners, including Lieberman, hold 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Palestinian minority, which hold 19 seats and ⁠are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.
Lieberman had once served as foreign minister under a previous Netanyahu government but has since become a strong critic.
Talks are also ongoing between Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.
The left-wing Democrats party, which won eight parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot after the Yashar party leader’s talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government.
Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, said he prefers a government without Netanyahu but with the Arab parties.

articles.title_orig: U.S. plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
articles.title_zh: U.S. plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump's administration is getting ready to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and a dozen other trading partners
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump's administration is planning to hike tariffs on Chinese goods by an additional 20% and raise import taxes on products from the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other major trading partners.
The new tariffs are meant to discourage excessive manufacturing output in those economies, boosted by subsidies and other trade barriers that the Republican administration says put American manufacturers at a disadvantage. The taxes are also intended to help replace the tariff revenues lost after the Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump could not declare an economic emergency to bypass Congress and impose across-the-board tariffs.
In a late-night call with reporters on Tuesday, a senior administration official provided details of the planned tariffs ahead of the release of a series of investigations into the trade practices of 12 countries, the 27-member EU and the self-governing island of Taiwan. The official insisted on anonymity as a condition for discussing the reports before they were posted by the U.S. Trade Representative's office.
The official stressed that the tariffs were still at the proposal stage and did not provide strict timelines on possible implementation.
The tariffs — rolled out early Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving — represent another controversial twist in Trump's economic policy. Voters in this month's midterm elections punished Republicans by handing majorities in the House and the Senate to Democrats, with about two-thirds of voters saying that Trump's policies had made the economy worse, according to The AP Voter Poll , a sweeping survey of the American electorate conducted in all 50 states.
Trump has promised that the import taxes will bring back manufacturing jobs and reduce the federal deficit, but last year's tariffs contributed to higher inflation that angered voters and led to calls by Democratic lawmakers to require congressional approval going forward.
The Trump administration argues that these countries have helped spur an influx of goods at lower prices that undercut American companies, creating a trade deficit in goods that has recently exceeded $1 trillion annually.
The legal basis of the planned tariffs is Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which enables the U.S. government to investigate and retaliate against foreign trade practices that violate existing deals, are not justified by market forces or actively discriminate against American goods. The official told reporters that the new tariffs would be consistent with the trade deals that Trump reached last year with dozens of countries after threatening severe tariff hikes .
Brazil was singled out for extra punishment after talks on trade issues stalled, the official said. The U.S. is proposing higher import taxes for raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft, a move that would hit Embraer, Brazil’s largest aircraft maker.
For some Chinese goods, the new 20% tariff will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.
The U.S. and China reached a trade truce last year that is set to expire on Jan. 10. The new tariffs will not come as a surprise to Beijing and are unlikely to undermine the truce, the administration official said.
Trump met last week in Shenzhen, China, with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and plans to host him next month at the Group of 20 summit in Florida, an event at which the truce and issues over access to rare earth minerals and China's purchases of American agricultural products could be discussed again.
The official stressed that the tariffs are targeted to specific products. They would not stack on top of separate tariffs on automobiles, steel, aluminum and other products that the administration has separately imposed under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.
Neither will they stack on top of levies of 10% to 12.5% announced in July for 60 trading partners that the White House said have inadequately enforced bans on goods produced by forced labor.
Other nations facing the new tariffs are Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Thailand and Vietnam. The official said there are two other countries with pending investigations: Mexico and Norway.
The Associated Press confirmed the planned tariff announcement ahead of the call, according to people who insisted on anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly. The plans were reported earlier on Tuesday by Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal.

articles.title_orig: Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman
articles.title_zh: Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman
articles.content_orig:
Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads.
Speaking on his latest Power On podcast , Gurman said there is "no work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad." Rather, Apple will continue to bring Mac features and apps like Final Cut to iPadOS piece by piece. Gurman also argued that per-operating-system EU regulation gives Apple an incentive to keep distinct systems for each device. Apple recently dismissed merging iPadOS and macOS.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine’s raid in Libya damaged more than a Russian warship
articles.title_zh: Ukraine’s raid in Libya damaged more than a Russian warship
articles.content_orig:
Jamie Dettmer is associate editor and a foreign affairs columnist for POLITICO.
Ukraine’s attack on a Russian warship in a Libyan port was a striking military success. It may also have broken international law.
“An exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war” was how Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy lauded Sunday’s sinking of the Merkury, one of Russia’s most advanced corvettes, docked at the time in Benghazi. Ukraine’s leader proudly announced on his Telegram channel that the operation, involving seven Ukrainian-made sea drones, had also disabled a Russian cargo ship suspected of transporting weapons.
From a military perspective the operation was indeed another one of Ukraine’s audacious commando missions. It was reminiscent of the derring-do spirit of Winston Churchill’s “Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare,” better known as the Special Operations Executive, which mounted commando raids along the French coast, causing havoc and raising British wartime morale during WWII .
In fact, the day before, while visiting Kyiv, Britain’s defense secretary Wes Streeting had coincidentally compared Zelenskyy to Britain’s iconic wartime leader.
The comparison was ironic given the circumstances. Despite Churchill’s impatience and determination to take the fight to the enemy, the wartime prime minister was careful to avoid breaching the laws of armed conflict at sea. He didn’t, for example, order British warships to sink the German cruiser Admiral Graf Spee when it was cornered in Montevideo after the Battle of the River Plate. The trapped warship’s captain ultimately decided to scuttle the ship.
But Zelenskyy wasn’t so restrained this week. According to international legal scholars, the attack likely violated international law as well as Libya’s sovereignty. The country’s eastern administration, based in Benghazi, has called on the U.N. to investigate the sinking as well as “reports regarding the presence of Ukrainian personnel, experts or military units” in western Libya.
The Libyans would have a good case if they lodged a complaint with the International Court of Justice, said David Letts, a retired Australian naval officer and now director of the military law program at the Australian National University in Canberra. “Unless you’re wanting to mount an argument that Libya is somehow involved in the conflict between Ukraine and Russia and neutrality doesn’t apply, I’m struggling to see how this sinking sits within the law,” Letts said.
Letts is one of the authors of the Newport Manual on the Law of Naval Warfare, a compilation of legislation published and updated by the U.S. Naval War College. He says Ukraine’s Benghazi attack is “quite different when compared to their strikes against Russian vessels in the Black Sea and in Black Sea ports” in disputed and not neutral waters.
The laws of neutrality are largely based on the 1907 Hague Convention, which codified the rights and duties of non-belligerent states during armed conflicts. Under it, countries at war are prohibited from conducting attacks, blockades or mine-laying within neutral waters. In return, neutral states shouldn’t let belligerent warships turn their ports into military bases. Stays are generally limited to 24 hours, with exceptions for damage, repairs or poor weather.
“The attack was a violation of Libya’s neutrality,” said James Kraska of the U.S. Naval War College and professor of international maritime law in the Stockton Center for International Law. “An attack is lawful if it’s beyond 12 nautical miles from the coastline, but, of course, inside it’s a violation.”
“Now on the Ukrainian side, what their argument might be is that a belligerent warship ought only to stay 24 hours in a foreign neutral port. If it goes beyond 24 hours, then the warship is at risk, and Libya might not be in compliance,” Kraska, a retired U.S. Navy commander, told POLITICO. “If there’s inclement weather, or repairs are needed to make it seaworthy, then the time can be extended,” he added. Some scholars, he added, would argue that Ukraine would need to contact the Libyan authorities to find out the status.
In terms of its boldness and reach, Monday’s attack wasn’t entirely unprecedented. In March, Libyan authorities reported damage to the Russian gas tanker Arctic Metagaz while it was en route to Egypt. Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the tanker with naval drones likely launched from Western Libya. Kyiv neither confirmed nor denied its involvement.
The governments of Sudan, Mali and Niger have also accused Ukrainian special forces of mounting operations in their countries, where Russian mercenary soldiers are present. Kyiv has denied those allegations.
This time, though, Kyiv has proudly admitted sinking the Merkury in a neutral port. Why? And does the breach of law on neutrality actually matter? Zelenskyy’s office didn’t respond to questions from POLITICO on the sinking, including as to whether it had sought counsel from senior government law officers before approving the attack, and whether it had notified Libyan authorities beforehand to request the ship leave Benghazi.
In the past, when questions of neutrality have arisen or Ukraine has been accused of breaching the laws of warfare, Kyiv has said this is no time for niceties as it is the aggrieved nation. When a U.N. monitoring mission in 2023 alleged abuse of Russian POWs, for example, the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry thanked the mission for documenting Russia’s violations but pushed back on the claims against Kyiv, arguing: “We consider it unacceptable to place responsibility on the victim of aggression.”
Former U.K. diplomat Tim Willasey-Wilsey, now a fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, a defense think tank in London with close ties to Ukraine’s defense ministry, says that when it comes to the sinking of the Merkury, he doesn’t believe the legal issues are important. “Who gives a stuff, really, you know? To be honest, I don’t think the legality particularly matters.”
He said the biggest political risk for Kyiv is diminishing the “remarkable degree of Western support for Ukraine,” and so was reassured when Wes Streeting came out so quickly in support. The attack, he said, reflected desperation in Ukraine, where ballistic missile attacks are devastating civilian infrastructure, itself a violation by Russia of international law. “The war is clearly getting more and more visceral, and I think the timing of the Benghazi attack is testimony to the sense of desperation that there is now in Kyiv.”
But turning a blind eye to the Benghazi attack only adds to the erosion of international legal norms and the undermining of the post-1945 “rules-based international order,” which Moscow and Beijing have little time for. It makes the seas more dangerous.
Letts stressed how important it is for countries like Ukraine to stick to what’s legal. “I wonder what the attitude would be if this vessel had been docked in Genoa or Southampton, say, rather than Benghazi,” he added. “I think there’s an element here of ‘It was only over there, so it doesn’t really matter.’”
“Having built up a body of law that tries to protect victims of armed conflict, tries to limit the scope of armed conflicts, are we willing to wave goodbye to all of that?” he asked. “Are we willing just to have total warfare with all the rules gone and to say, ‘The last 100 years or so are a waste of time. Do whatever you want.’ I don’t think we are.”

articles.title_orig: Gold Holds Decline as US Tariff Plans Reinforce Rate-Hike Bets
articles.title_zh: Gold Holds Decline as US Tariff Plans Reinforce Rate-Hike Bets
articles.content_orig:
Gold fell more than ​2% to its ​lowest level in more ​than a year after strong U.S. inflation data failed to assuage concerns surrounding the Federal Reserve's rate-hike path.
Spot gold was down 2% to $3,483.59 an ounce, falling to its lowest ⁠level since September 2025. U.S. gold futures for December delivery dropped 2.3% to $3,482.50.
US inflation increased further in October, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index rising 0.3% after an unrevised 0.5% ‌gain in September, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said on Wednesday.
"With inflationary pressures remaining significantly above the Fed ​target, the likelihood continues that the Fed will raise interest rates moving forward, which adds pressure to gold," said David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures.
"That's been one ⁠of the main themes that remains a headwind for the gold market, and today's ‌PCE data did nothing to allay those concerns."
Elevated ‌rates tend to diminish the attractiveness of non-yielding gold relative to interest-bearing assets.
Markets have fully priced in a rate hike at the US central bank's December ⁠policy meeting, according to the CME's FedWatch tool. The Fed last ⁠raised rates in September.
Spot gold prices have tumbled roughly ⁠37% since hitting a record high earlier this year.
Meanwhile, the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell ​more than expected last week, pointing ‌to stable labor market conditions.
On the geopolitical front, U.S. President Donald Trump reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on major trading powers including China, undeterred in his protectionist push by his Republican Party's losses in midterm elections.
Among ​other metals, spot silver fell 3.8% ‌to $39.33 an ounce, platinum slid 2.7% to $1,241.67 and palladium lost 1.7% to $838.61.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft declares “Code Red” after huge Outlook outage
articles.title_zh: Microsoft declares “Code Red” after huge Outlook outage
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is now holding daily meetings with the engineering group responsible for Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft is now holding daily meetings with the engineering group responsible for Microsoft 365 services.
This month’s Exchange Online and Microsoft Outlook outage has prompted the software giant to declare an unusual “Code Red” internally, Reuters reports . The nearly 24-hour outage took down email for millions of customers, and was triggered by a bug that had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers.
In a memo to the teams responsible for Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson revealed the outage was the most significant in history for Microsoft’s customers. “Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday,” said Henderson. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team.”
As part of this Code Red declaration, Microsoft is focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning, and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft now has a target of resolving future outages within an hour, and will reportedly deploy AI agents to help engineers diagnose issues. Microsoft is now holding daily meetings with the engineering group responsible for Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly reviews.
In a separate memo, Amanda Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers had to work through a “fog of war” to help resolve the outage. I reported last week that Microsoft engineers had a running bridge call during the entire outage, and at one point it hit the maximum of 1,000 participants.
Microsoft engineers had to exchange messages across 11 Teams chats and reportedly “struggled ​to maintain a cohesive picture” during the outage because of the fragmented internal tracking systems. Sources tell me the outage was marked as “sev0,” the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Engineers struggled to get servers back online because they had entered maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads.

articles.title_orig: Dell Delivered Strong Earnings but at the Wrong Time for the Stock
articles.title_zh: Dell Delivered Strong Earnings but at the Wrong Time for the Stock
articles.content_orig:
Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.
Dell shares rose in extended trading.
Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
Dell said that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue.
The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand.
The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD .
ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue.
"We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers.
In prepared remarks, Clarke said that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery.
"That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably," Clarke said in the prepared remarks published by Dell.
The company also raised its forecast for AI-servers in the coming fiscal year to $78 billion, versus $74 billion expected. The company says it has a backlog of $132.3 billion in AI server orders it is working through.
"Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power," Clarke said on an earnings call with analysts.
The company also sells laptops and PCs, in a group it calls CSG, or client services group. It reported $12.89 billion in sales, which was below LSEG expectations of $14.33 billion.
The overall PC market has been getting whacked of late, with some estimates calling the lull the worst ever, as rising memory prices have led to higher device prices and consumers are choosing to hang on to their old laptops longer.
Dell said that it had authorized $25 billion in share repurchases, and that it had spent $4.9 billion in the third quarter on share repurchases and dividends.
Dell shares are up over 135% so far in 2026.

articles.title_orig: 'I'm going to drive': FAA outage and high fares reshape Thanksgiving travel plans
articles.title_zh: 'I'm going to drive': FAA outage and high fares reshape Thanksgiving travel plans
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Doyinsola Oladipo and David Shepardson
NEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Dinese Jackson couldn't stomach spending roughly $1,500 to fly herself and her two children from Raleigh, North Carolina, to Dallas, Texas, for Thanksgiving, more than double what she had paid for similar trips in the past.
Still, she kept checking airfares in hopes fares would ‌drop, until the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop on November 13 cemented her decision to make the trip by car instead, even at the price of a ‌17-hour drive.
"When that happened on Friday, I was like, 'Yep, I'm keeping my car reservation. I'm going to go ahead and drive for sure," the 51-year-old credit analyst told Reuters. "For those that are flying, I just think it's going to be ​chaos."
A router outage on November 13 caused a communications failure at air traffic control centers and triggered a nearly five-hour nationwide disruption impacting more than 18,000 flights and affecting about 1 million passengers.
Just a few days later, travelers faced fresh disruptions when United Airlines suffered a widespread technology outage and Delta Air Lines' automated weight-and-balance system failed on Sunday, delaying more than 2,000 flights nationwide, shaking confidence in air travel ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The rising cost of airfare, which has hit 10-year highs for the holiday period, had already persuaded some Americans to stay home this year. Airlines for America ‌forecast nearly 29 million passengers will travel between November 20 and 30, ⁠down from last year's forecast of 31 million passengers.
HIGHEST AIRFARE IN A DECADE
Two weeks before Thanksgiving, domestic airfares for the holiday travel period averaged about $469 in 2026, about a 57% year-over-year increase, according to data from travel search engine, Kayak. Travel booking app Hopper said months of elevated jet ⁠fuel costs due to the conflict in Iran have helped push Thanksgiving and Christmas fares to 10-year highs.
United Airlines said it expects more than 6.6 million customers over a 12-day period, on par with last year. American Airlines said it plans to welcome 8 million travelers in the same period, and plans to operate 4% more flights than in 2025. US airlines are operating 2% more flights on average this Thanksgiving than ​last ​year, while seat capacity is up 1%, Cirium, a flight analytics company, said.
Fewer Americans are traveling by air in 2026 ​as fares rise and disruptions mount. The last time the Transportation Security ‌Administration screened more than 3 million passengers in a single day was November 30, 2025. The TSA has not screened 3 million passengers on any day this year, compared to eight times in 2025.
During the Thanksgiving Holiday, the agency expects to screen about 3% fewer passengers year-on-year.
Jennifer Shaw, 57, was less than thrilled to learn her son planned to forfeit his non-refundable plane ticket home from college in Michigan. Instead, he opted to drive 10 hours to Monmouth County, New Jersey, with friends rather than risk getting stranded at an airport during the holiday rush.
"Even though I might be worried that he's driving 10 hours with a group of boys, at least I don't have to worry about the airlines," Shaw said.
The FAA warned stormy weather could affect flights ‌throughout the week.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said last week the agency was "very close" to being ​able to disclose the root cause of the router outage. The FAA declined to say Monday when it plans ​to offer an update.
On November 17, the FAA said it had immediately paused deployment of ​additional routers.
"I'm hoping the government is not going to do any more upgrades during this time that we're going to be away," said retiree Liz ‌Dougherty, 63, who plans to fly from North Carolina to Spain to ​take a cruise for the holiday, adding that ​the November 13 flight halt was "definitely in the back of my mind."
About 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving over a six-day period, according to AAA estimates, down only slightly from last year's total of 81.6 million. However, more Americans are expected to take cruises, buses, and trains to their destinations.
Bus and travel search engine, ​Wanderu, said the ground stop gave the company its busiest day ‌of the year so far, with bookings made that Friday up about 16% from last year. Bus operator Flix North America said bookings for Thanksgiving are up 17% ​from last year.
Amtrak said the company is again expecting a record in 2026 after 1.2 million customer trips during last year's Thanksgiving holiday.
(Reporting by Doyinsola Oladipo in ​New York, additional reporting by David Shepardson in Washington; Editing by Christian Plumb and Aurora Ellis)

articles.title_orig: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed chip giant to reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed chip giant to reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
President Trump holds tens of millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride over the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.
Mr. Trump stood to lose large sums with CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure, and stood to profit handsomely after he successfully pressed the chip developer's board to reinstate Huang. Nvidia stock surged more than 30% when Huang returned to the company on Monday, reversing a weekslong slide.
Huang resigned two weeks ago over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who ran a company accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China, and another alleged affair with a subordinate. Mr. Trump said Monday he personally spoke with Nvidia's board and "convinced them" to rehire Huang, offering an "assurance" that there was no national security threat.
Mr. Trump held between $13 million and $58 million in Nvidia stock in his investment accounts as of the end of 2025, according to financial disclosures filed with the Office of Government Ethics. He bought or sold the company's stock in more than 100 transactions that were worth between $27 million and nearly $98 million between January 2025 and September 2026.
The value of the president's Nvidia shares increased anywhere from $1.3 million to $14.8 million on Monday, before paring back some of those gains when Nvidia's share price ticked down Tuesday. The range is so large because it isn't clear how many shares of Nvidia the president currently owns, but it can be roughly estimated based on his sales and purchases this year.
"President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions," a White House spokesman told CBS News Tuesday, adding that his investments mirror indexes like the Schwab 1000. "Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers."
In addition to the president, several of his appointees to positions in the State, Commerce and Treasury departments as well as the IRS reported millions in Nvidia stock in their investment portfolios. Many have since sold their holdings.
Forbes estimates Mr. Trump's net worth at more than $6 billion, making Nvidia a small part of his total wealth. And Nvidia is one of the world's most valuable public companies, at more than $3.7 trillion, so many investors hold shares in the tech giant.
Still, some ethics experts questioned Mr. Trump's large stake in Nvidia, especially after he intervened to boost the company's fortunes.
"This goes beyond a conflict of interest," said Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "He is squarely, explicitly using his power as president to benefit himself financially. He has prioritized his finances over the security of the nation."
Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit government watchdog, told CBS News that Mr. Trump's "continued ownership of stock in this company is the clearest example of how the president's personal financial interest makes everything he does suspect."
Mr. Trump's personal investments have drawn controversy in the past, including his stakes in publicly traded energy companies, firms that have business with the government and his family's cryptocurrency firm . He has denied any conflict of interest.
Some critics called for legal reforms to prohibit the president and members of Congress from buying and selling stocks while they hold office. Elected officials are generally allowed to trade individual stocks, though lawmakers from both parties have called for the practice to be banned.
Richard Painter, a law professor at the University of Minnesota and former chief ethics attorney for the White House between 2005 and 2007, said he has long argued for changes to the federal conflict of interest law that prohibits government employees from participating in matters that result in their personal enrichment while in office. That current law does not apply to the president, vice president or members of Congress, he said.
"We need a prohibition on this right away," he said, adding that the new Congress may take up the cause in January.
Painter called Mr. Trump's intervention with the Nvidia board "a huge conflict of interest" and overreach of government power.
"It's not the job of the government to call up and say who the CEO of a company should be," he told CBS News.
The president has defended his decision to intervene , saying on CNBC that "we have to protect our geniuses" and arguing that Nvidia — as the world's leading designer of advanced chips — plays a key role in maintaining the U.S.' lead over China in AI technology.
Mr. Trump has also frequently pointed to the performance of the stock market as a barometer of his success as president. Shortly after Huang was reinstated, Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal the "response from the market has been very positive," and "that really shows the decision was right."
Beyond Mr. Trump, numerous political appointees held Nvidia stock. Some divested themselves of their holdings after they were appointed to government positions, federal filings show.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin owned between $250,000 and $500,000 in Nvidia stock in March 2026, and sold $500,000 to $1 million in shares of the tech company in June of this year, his financial disclosures show.
"As Secretary of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin acts to ensure full compliance with all ethics and conflict of interest rules," said a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security.
In the Commerce Department, where Secretary Howard Lutnick is facing scrutiny over whether he has done enough to crack down on highly sensitive AI chip sales to China, a number of senior advisers last year reported selling large positions in Nvidia.
Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm that was previously run by Lutnick and is now controlled by his sons, reported holding roughly 1 million shares of Nvidia for its clients as of Sept. 30, worth around $228 million at the time. Those shares were worth just over $150 million at Tuesday's price. None of Lutnick's personal financial disclosures filed by the federal government mention Nvidia holdings or transactions.
In the State Department, some of Mr. Trump's diplomatic appointees had Nvidia holdings.
Charles Kushner, the U.S. ambassador to France and father of Mr. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, reported Nvidia holdings totaling between $1.5 million and $6 million, according to public disclosures filed January 2025.
U.S. Ambassador to Costa Rica Melinda Hildebrand reported Nvidia holdings between $5 million and $25 million, her April 2025  disclosures show. The Texas billionaire, who was a major Trump campaign fundraiser, sold the stock in November of that same year, filings show.
Warren Stephens, another major Trump donor and ambassador to the United Kingdom, reported Nvidia holdings between $750,000 and $1.5 million, according to his January 2025  disclosures. He sold those shares in July and August 2025, a few months after he was sworn in as ambassador.
In the Treasury Department, Under Secretary for International Affairs Erin Browne held Nvidia shares totaling between $250,000 and $500,000, her disclosures from January show. Browne sold the stock before her confirmation in August of this year, filings show.
Todd Newnam, who was appointed chief financial officer of the IRS in January, holds between $115,000 and $250,000 in Nvidia stock, according to his financial disclosure, filed in April of last year. Newnam, a former CEO of a tech company, was part of the Department of Government Efficiency team that sought to streamline government spending and cut the federal workforce.

articles.title_orig: I think Apple's $700 iPad mini beats its $2,000 iPhone Duo in one important way
articles.title_zh: I think Apple's $700 iPad mini beats its $2,000 iPhone Duo in one important way
articles.content_orig:
The iPhone Duo's folding design features two displays that introduce several new ways to use an iPhone. Over the past few weeks, we've covered the best of them, from Split View multitasking to hands-free group photos.
If you're lucky enough to be an iPhone Duo owner, we've collected the 20 top tips worth trying below. Full tutorials for each tip can be found in our how-to section .
Unfold your iPhone Duo so that it's in landscape orientation, then swipe up from the bottom. Drag an app to the left or right edge, and then tap a second app to make it fill the other side. You can also touch and hold an app icon and tap Open in Split View. The split is fixed at 50/50, and only one app plays audio at a time.
With two apps open in Split View, simply tap the divider between them to ensure they always launch together. If you change your mind, drag the divider fully to either edge of the screen to unpair them.
This one requires iOS 27.3, which is currently in beta. With your Duo closed, swipe left on the left edge of the outer display to bring the right side of the screen within reach, and vice versa. Note that it's on by default after updating to the beta (control it via Settings ➝ Accessibility ➝ Touch ➝ Reachability) and it works on the outer display only.
Rotating to portrait normally drops Split View to one app, but Apple has provided a workaround. Start a video in a Picture in Picture-supporting app like Apple TV or Podcasts, then tap the PiP icon, swipe up to the Home Screen, open the second app (it can't be another video app), and tap the newly visible stack icon in the PiP window to dock the video above it.
The iPhone Duo has no Ring/Silent switch and no Action button that you can assign to silence your iPhone. The quickest alternative is to invoke Control Center and tap the Silent Mode bell. If the control is missing, add it via the plus button ➝ Add a Control. You'll find it under the Sounds category. Note that alarms and media audio will still play in Silent mode.
Tap the circular status bar immediately below the clock – the combined Wi-Fi, cellular, and battery indicator – instead of stretching for the top corner to swipe down Control Center. It sits even lower when a Live Activity is running, so it's often easier to reach one-handed. It also makes silencing the phone with the mute control a two-tap job.
With your Duo unfolded in landscape orientation, tap the More (...) button at the top-left of the keyboard, then tap Split for a more comfortable typing experience. Don't like it? Simply choose More ➝ Full to rejoin the layout. Another tip to remember is that when your Duo is closed, you can long-press the globe or emoji key to shift the keyboard to one side for easier one-handed typing.
In Settings ➝ StandBy, you can tick the folding positions that you want, and if you keep Only While Charging switched off, you can enjoy your StandBy modes without a charger having to be plugged in. When you lock the phone, half-fold it like a book or make it into a tent shape it on a flat surface, StandBy will start automatically.
In Shortcuts, you can create an automation with the Opened or Closed trigger plus the Open App action, and your chosen app will automatically launch whenever you unfold the phone . For example, if you choose the Kindle app, unfolding the Duo feels like opening a book. You can also constrain it with conditions like time of day or Focus.
This one requires the iOS 27.3 beta 2, but it's a good one. If you authenticate into Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode, and toggle on the new Face Unlock option, you can unlock the device with the front camera. It only works at the Lock Screen when the Duo is closed, so you can't use it for authenticating Apple Pay purchases or inserting logins and passwords from the Passwords app. You also need to use Touch ID or a passcode for unlocking the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's unfolded.
The toggle in Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode (also in Settings ➝ Accessibility ➝ Side Button) lets you open the phone straight past the Lock Screen, simply by resting your finger on the side button while the screen is awake. No more needing to swipe up to access the Home Screen.
Unfold your iPhone Duo, open the Camera app, then turn the phone around and drag the Show Camera slider on the outer display. You'll get the 48-megapixel rear Fusion cameras with a live preview on the side facing you, plus you can shoot with the on-screen shutter button, a volume button, or Camera Control.
Next time you're on a group FaceTime call and someone in the room wants to join in, simply tap the screen, tap the More button, then tap Duo FaceTime. The makes the person next to you get their own view via the Center Stage front camera and the under-display camera, meaning nobody has to squeeze into the same frame.
Found in Control Center, Orientation Lock on the iPhone Duo applies only to the display you're using when you enable it, so the outer display can stay locked in portrait while the inner display rotates freely. Note that videos will still rotate automatically in tent mode, regardless of the lock.
Go to Settings ➝ Sounds & Haptics, and turn off Fixed Position Volume Controls. The top or right button is then always volume up, whichever way you are holding the phone. Apple's documentation suggests this dynamic behavior is the default, but that hasn't been the case on the early units we've tested.
If you enable the toggle next to Settings ➝ Display & Brightness ➝ Shift Left Edge, it will inset the outer display so that your case doesn't cover on-screen content. Apple's official case prompts you to enable it, but you can also turn it on manually if you have a third-party case.
If you have an Apple Watch, this tip is an absolute game-changer. Go to Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode ➝ Unlock with Nearby Devices and toggle on your watch model. With the watch on your wrist (and unlocked), wake the Duo and swipe up, and the watch is your authentication – no Touch ID required.
When lining up a shot in the Camera app, tap the Outer Display Options button and choose Duo Preview, and your subject will see a mirrored live preview on the outer display while you frame it up. You can do it for both photos and video.
Prop your iPhone Duo somewhere steady, tap the Smart Take button in the Camera pp, and get in the frame. The device will capture automatically when you pose or hold still, and can take up to 20 photos. If you have it half-folded on its side, one half of the screen becomes the viewfinder and the other shows the shots that have already been taken.
In the Camera app, Outer Display Options ➝ Kid Cue plays a Snoopy animation on the outer display to draw your subject's gaze while you frame them on the inner display. It's a good way to keep them looking at you for the ideal shot. The only trade-off is that they will appear like they are looking slightly off to the side, since it uses the main camera on the other hand of the phone.

articles.title_orig: Nine quick fixes for family tech problems this Thanksgiving
articles.title_zh: Nine quick fixes for family tech problems this Thanksgiving
articles.content_orig:
Home for the holidays? These steps will help you solve technology problems your parents or other family members might be having and prevent crises before they happen. They will make your life better too.
For millions of Americans spending time with family this Thanksgiving, their holiday visit will be greeted with an inevitable request: to fix gadgets around the house that aren't working like they should.
Tech support is part of the responsibility that comes with ageing parents for a lot of people I know. That isn't true in every family, of course (my dad has always been obsessed with computers. That's probably where I get it). But it got me thinking – maybe this Thanksgiving can be an opportunity to be proactive, rather than waiting for things to break.
Here are nine simple tech fixes to make everyone's digital lives safer, simpler and less annoying.
And if nothing else, a bit of light tech support will give you something to do as you loaf around between gut-busting meals on those bleary holiday afternoons.
Modern TVs usually have "motion smoothing" features on by default. These use AI to reduce the blur of quick-moving objects. It's great for sports, but it adds a surreal, plasticky appearance that makes everything look like a soap opera. Turn it off for better image quality. TVs use different names: look for "motion", "blur" or "smoothing" controls under display settings.
Here's the simple answer: move the router. Imagine a straight-line between the router and the area where you need signal. Move it off the ground, put it in a central area and avoid walls, doors and furniture. Some objects, like mirrors, metal surfaces and even fish tanks can be especially problematic. If all else fails, consider mesh routers or wi-fi extenders.
Forget reading out passwords letter by letter. iPhone and Android devices let you create a QR code that guests can scan with their phone camera to connect automatically.
• On iPhones, open the Passwords app > Wi-Fi > select your network > Show Network QR code .
• On Samsung phones, find it under Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi . You can save QR code as an image or print it out and stick it to the fridge.
• On Android, select Network and Internet > Internet > tap Settings next to your wi-fi network > Share.
While you're at it, change your wi-fi password and network name to something easier to say and remember – using the default can leave you vulnerable to hacking. You just need to login to your router's admin settings or its companion app. You can usually find details on the back of the router or just look up the model.
Older people are particularly vulnerable to scams and fraud, but thanks to ever growing AI deepfakes, everyone is a potential victim. There's a simple solution to this problem: your family needs a secret codeword that you ask for over the phone in unusual situations. But creating the codeword is just step one. Check out our guide for everything you need to know.
Want to know more about the stories behind your screen? Check out the latest episode of The Interface , the BBC's flagship technology podcast.
Hearing loss can make movies and shows hard to follow. Some TVs and streaming services have special features for this, check for settings like "Clear Voice", "Dialogue Enhancer" or "Speech Mode". Switch off sound features like bass boost, virtual surround and cinema mode which can muddy voices. Use "standard" or "voice" mode instead.
If you haven't set up the "Find My" feature on your devices, you're begging for trouble. Apple devices have built in trackers that show where they are on a map when enabled . In some cases you can use the feature to trigger a sound so you can track the device down. Android has a network called the Find Hub , which works similarly. You can use these systems with other trackers you can clip on to anything from keys to wallets to remotes.
You've surely noticed that websites across the internet beg you to let them send your browser notifications. For some people it may sound convenient, but it can be a nuisance. Some shady websites can also use these pop-up notifications to scam people with warnings about fake viruses. You may be better off disabling them altogether or at least removing websites that aren't obviously reputable.
• Safari: go to Settings > Websites > Notifications > deselect " Allow websites to ask for permission to send notifications ".
• Chrome: click the three-dot menu, then Settings > Privacy and Security > Site Settings > Notifications > hit " Don't allow sites to send notifications " to block them all.
• The most important Google setting you aren ' t using
• The secret code words that spammers hate
• The weirdest things that mess up your wi-fi
Password managers don't just keep you safe, they make life simpler. You just memorise one master password, and the app will fill in other credentials automatically as you visit apps and websites. Casey Oppenheim, chief executive at Disconnect, a cybersecurity company, tells me he recommends using the password managers built into your phone and browser. Start with your most important and sensitive accounts, such as email, banking and health care. Some sites even let you use passkeys and skip typing passwords altogether. Hallelujah.
If you're getting storage warnings, there's a better option than paying for extra space in the cloud. Your phone is almost certainly full of a bunch of junk you don't need, and Apple and Android both have options to help pulverise it.
• On iPhone: Settings > General > iPhone Storage . From there, you can use the "Offload Unused Apps" and "Remove downloaded media" settings to find and delete large files, many of which you aren't going to need.
• On Android: Settings > Storage > Free up space . From there, use the category lists (such as downloads, large files and unused apps) to delete big, unnecessary files. Turn on "Smart Storage" to clear backed-up photos and videos automatically.
For more insights, sign up to our Tech Decoded newsletter, where Thomas and Lily Jamali break down the biggest stories of the tech world, and help you live a better digital life. Sign up for free here .

articles.title_orig: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.title_zh: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.content_orig:
FILE - Chen Jining, Communist Party Secretary for Shanghai attends a deliberation on the government work report, on the sideline of the National People's Congress at the Beijing Hotel, March 6, 2025. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption
BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.
A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.
The decision sent "a clear and powerful signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat," but with "a firm determination to win," the statement said.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong's rule.
"The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. "This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented."
The recent Politburo purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, with even officials with qualities that Xi apparently valued being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington.
"On paper," they appear to be "individuals Xi would appreciate," Torigian said, but afterward, "we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them."
Other Politburo members purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission, which oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
The post of Shanghai party secretary has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership. The country's former President Jiang Zemin, its current premier, Li Qiang, and Xi himself previously held the position.
Chen has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022. He previously held senior positions in Beijing's municipal government and headed the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

articles.title_orig: Russia’s Grip On Crimea Much Weaker After Key Waterways Blocked
articles.title_zh: Russia’s Grip On Crimea Much Weaker After Key Waterways Blocked
articles.content_orig:
Home » Russia’s Grip On Crimea Much Weaker After Key Waterways Blocked
Ukraine’s major attack on the Kerch Bridge, combined with a less-reported October strike on a bridge over the Don River, has effectively cut off the Sea of Azov. This makes it much harder for Russia to resupply Crimea.
8 years ago, on the 25th November 2018, Russia blocked the waterway under the Kerch Bridge to prevent Ukrainian ships accessing the Sea of Azov. At the time, despite a 2003 agreement guaranteeing free access to both countries to the Sea of Azov, Russia held the cards. Today the waterway under the Kerch bridge is again blocked, but this time it is different.
Ukraine’s successful attacks on the Kerch Bridge on 17th November have effectively severed the road link between Crimea and Russia. But it is much worse than that for Russia.
The collapsed bridge is blocking the shipping canal under the bridge. Combined with another less well-publicised attack on the rail bridge in Rostov on Don on 10th October , this greatly contributes to cutting off Crimea. At the time the strike was reported to have affected rail traffic, but the greater impact was on shipping. The port of Azov has essentially ceased operations. So both bridge attacks stop vital waterways at either end of the Sea of Azov, making it much harder for Russia to resupply Crimea.
The Crimean Peninsula, which Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014, is effectively becoming an island. The overland supply routes through the occupied territories in southern Ukraine are under constant and substantial air threat. They also rely on smaller bridges at both ends of the route which have repeatedly been disabled by Ukrainian strikes. And at the southern end, the Kerch Road bridge to Russia is now destroyed. The rail bridge still stands, but it is damaged and remains under threat.
Ukraine has been increasing its attacks along the road connection to northern Crimea. The M14 highway has been colloquially nicknamed the ‘ highway of death ’. Several low bridges have been struck at its eastern end near Rostov, and the Chonhar bridge at the Crimea end has been seriously damaged in previous attacks. Traffic is currently being rerouted across a temporary crossing.
The simplistic solution for Russia is to switch to shipping to keep the peninsula supplied. But this is where the strikes on the two bridges, combined with a major drone campaign against shipping starting in June, greatly impede this. That campaign which used mid-strike aerial drones to target shipping, codenamed Operation ‘Molochka’ meaning ‘ Moscow will fall because of Crimea ’, saw around 300 vessels hit . Shipping had already significantly decreased in the Sea of Azov even before the Kerch bridge was felled.
The October attack on the rail bridge over the Don River in Rostov also plays a part. Ukrainian strike drones appear to have targeted the lifting mechanisms, with footage of the attack showing impacts high up in its steel lattice structure. Information seen by Naval News indicates that the bridge was disabled, meaning that it can no longer be raised to allow ships to pass underneath. Only small vessels have passed under it since the attack.
So with both ends now blocked, the Sea of Azov has effectively become a closed lake. Only ships already in it will be able to be used for resupply from the east. And they will rely on road and rail networks to be loaded in ports. There are also only two viable ports, Krym and Kerch, on the Sea of Azov side of Crimea. Both are near the Kerch bridge and subject to frequent strikes. Maritime logistics in the Black Sea are similarly restricted.
The increasingly strained logistics, combined with fuel shortages and major energy outages make Russia’s grip on Crimea appear ever weaker. The peninsula is likely to become more of a focus over the coming months.
